intro.title: Container queries
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive card component that adapts its layout based on the size of its container, not just the viewport. You will learn the core concept of container queries, a modern CSS feature that allows elements to respond to their parent container's dimensions. The main technologies involved are CSS container queries, using properties like container-type and container-name, and the @container rule. This approach provides more flexible and modular responsive design compared to traditional media queries.
intro.usecase: Container queries solve a common problem in modern web development: components that need to adapt their layout based on their available space, not just the viewport. You'll see this in product dashboards where sidebar panels, data cards, and metric widgets resize intelligently as users drag divider handles or collapse navigation menus. News websites use container queries for article grids that flow differently in main content areas versus narrower sidebars. E-commerce sites apply them to product cards that display more details when placed in wide containers but show compact versions in filtered result lists. This allows developers to create truly reusable components that work anywhere in the interface without media query duplication.
